__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Select the Prometheus data source that scrapes 10.12.1.31:11090.

description: Keycloak 12 / WildFly server monitoring using the exact base_*, vendor_* and wildfly_* metrics provided from 10.12.1.31:11090/metrics. No custom Grafana plugins or recording rules required. Authentication event and user-session metrics are not available in the supplied endpoint.

options.content:
**Target:** `$instance` · **Prometheus job:** `$job` · **Metrics path:** `/metrics`

JVM, WildFly, HTTP listeners and KeycloakDS monitoring, matched to the supplied metrics. **Scrape UP** means Prometheus can collect metrics; it does not test login availability. HTTP and database statistics were all zero in the supplied snapshot: check statistics collection if they remain zero during application traffic. Login events and realm user-session counts are not present in the supplied metrics.

panels.title: Metrics scrape
panels.description: 1 = most recent Prometheus scrape succeeded; 0 = scrape failed. Missing data is shown separately. This does not verify the Keycloak login flow.

panels.title: JVM uptime
panels.description: Time since the JVM started, in seconds.

panels.title: JVM process CPU
panels.description: JVM process CPU load fraction multiplied by 100. This is not host CPU utilization. Unsupported negative readings are omitted.

panels.title: Heap used / maximum
panels.description: Heap used as a percentage of maximum heap. Thresholds are starting points for review, not alert rules.

panels.title: Live JVM threads
panels.description: Current live JVM thread count.

panels.title: DB connections in use
panels.description: Connections currently borrowed from KeycloakDS. Zero can mean no usage or disabled pool statistics; it is not a database health check.

panels.title: Heap memory
panels.description: Heap memory reported by the JVM.

panels.title: Non-heap memory
panels.description: Non-heap memory includes metaspace and compiled code. Undefined or negative maximum values are omitted.

panels.title: JVM process CPU
panels.description: Reported JVM CPU fraction, converted to percent. This metric is not node CPU utilization.

panels.title: Garbage collections / minute
panels.description: Per-collector counter increase normalized to a minute. Rate graphs need multiple scrapes.

panels.title: Garbage collection time
panels.description: Collection elapsed seconds per wall-clock second. This is not an individual-pause latency histogram.

panels.title: JVM memory pools
panels.description: Memory pool names match the JVM and collector in the supplied snapshot. These names may change after JVM or GC changes.

panels.title: System load average
panels.description: Operating-system load average is not CPU percent. The processor count is shown only as a reference.

panels.title: Listener requests / second
panels.description: Selects only series with a server label, excluding the servlet counter to avoid double-counting. Includes all requests on the selected listeners, not just logins.

panels.title: Listener errors / second
panels.description: Undertow listener error counter. This is not a failed-login count or a complete HTTP status-code breakdown.

panels.title: Mean listener processing time
panels.description: Rate of total listener processing time divided by request rate. No requests produces no value. This is a mean, not p95 or p99.

panels.title: Listener network throughput
panels.description: Application listener throughput, not host-interface network traffic.

panels.title: KeycloakDS connections
panels.description: Pool statistics. Available capacity can include connections that could be created and must not be interpreted as idle physical connections. All-zero values in an active environment warrant checking statistics-enabled.

panels.title: KeycloakDS waits and failures
panels.description: Raw accumulated pool statistics, exported as gauges by this endpoint. Values can reset after restart or statistics reset.

panels.title: I/O worker threads
panels.description: Current thread counts reported by the default I/O worker.

panels.title: Work queues
panels.description: Queued work can help diagnose thread saturation. Zero is a normal value when no work is queued.
